answer: To open an earning key, an operator books one licensed kiln firing and hangs a uniquely poured copper coupon in the stack so the furnace plume lays a one-way oxide film on that coupon alone. The still-warm coupon is then pressed to a catalogued museum relic, co-absorbing a trace of the relic's surface oil into the film. Clones collide because one coupon can carry only one film, and one relic appointment cannot be kept in two kilns at once; an attacker must buy a new firing, pour a new coupon, and book a separate relic pressing for every extra key.
